ashley: Ran the SM capability sweep on nv-pproxy (inst-x). Getting inconsistent BF16/FP8 flags across the pool. Dump: 
```
GPU0 SM=80 tensorcore=true bf16=false fp8=unknown
GPU1 SM=80 tensorcore=true bf16=true fp8=false
GPU2 SM=86 tensorcore=true bf16=true fp8=true
```
jonathan: weird, driver mismatch or early probe race. Did you run nvidia-smi + cuobjdump on the affected nodes? :eyes:
ashley: nvidia-smi shows driver 525.85 on all nodes. cuobjdump returns different PTX capabilities on some. Also perf-bot raised a regression for long sequences (2048): p99 latency spike ~2.3x.
perf-bot: ALERT: kernel-pick fallback on inst-x. Requests with sequence_len>=1024 landed on generic_gemm path instead of tensorcore-optimized path -> p99 +130%.
luis: this smells like a capability cache TTL issue. If our probe runs before the driver fully exposes capabilities we cache false negatives. We've seen this with container restarts. Suggest adding a short reprobe delay before persisting capabilities.
sasha: also our probe order currently is bf16 -> fp8 -> tensorcore. If bf16 probe fails we skip some tensorcore-specialized kernels that could still run with fp16. Maybe reorder to tensorcore first, then bf16/fp8.
jonathan: agree. We should also allow a "partial" probe result to trigger a scheduled reprobe instead of immediate cache write.
nashley: quick patch idea:
```diff
- probe_order = ["bf16","fp8","tensorcore"]
+ probe_order = ["tensorcore","bf16","fp8"]
+ if probe_result.partial:
+   schedule_reprobe(2000)  # ms
```
luis: another angle: KV cache allocation granularity. For seqlen > 512 we allocate in 64k chunks; on some SM80 variants that causes extra memcpy+align penalties. Trying 4k pages for large KV reduces memcpy overhead.
sasha: canary? I can route 10% traffic to sm-tune branch with the reprobe+reorder patches. Want to watch both long-seq p99 and small-seq throughput.
ashley: launching canary now. Will post graphs in ~15m. :rocket:
ops: noted, expect some cold-start reprobes and brief extra NVML queries. We'll watch node stability. @ops
jonathan: FYI, adding a re-probe backoff so we don't hammer NVML on large clusters. If reprobe_count>3 mark as "degraded" and fallback to soft-heuristic.
nashley: 15m update: canary shows p99 for long-seq back to baseline, reprobe fixed the mismatch. Small-seq throughput dropped ~5% due to added checks.
luis: fine tradeoff but we should make reprobe conditional: only run for nodes that hit the long-seq fallback. I'll add a histogram-based gate (p95_smallseq < threshold => skip reprobe). Opening PR.
nashley: filing issue #3582 and PR #5603 for probe reorder + reprobe-on-partial. Thanks all. :+1:
